# Snapshot140 input/HIGH allocation order

## Result

Removing the stale `buffer_addr`/`src_cursor` setup changes which pseudo owns
the first use of `D_800E3E48`.  That gives the naturally hoisted HIGH one extra
reference.  GCC's global-allocation priority has a `floor_log2(refs)` factor,
so the change from three to four references more than doubles the HIGH's score
and narrowly moves it ahead of the input-state pseudo:

| candidate | pseudo | refs | live length | priority | allocation order | hard register |
|---|---|---:|---:|---:|---|---|
| indexed source | input 81 | 7 | 123 | 1138 | before HIGH | s6 / 22 |
| indexed source | HIGH 144 | 3 | 70 | 428 | after input | s7 / 23 |
| live only | input 81 | 7 | 122 | 1147 | after HIGH | s7 / 23 |
| live only | HIGH 141 | 4 | 68 | 1176 | before input | s6 / 22 |

The relevant formula, with both pseudos occupying one SI hard register, is:

```text
priority = int(floor_log2(refs) * refs / live_length * 10000 * size)

indexed source:
  input81 = int(2 * 7 / 123 * 10000) = 1138
  HIGH144 = int(1 * 3 /  70 * 10000) =  428

live only:
  input81 = int(2 * 7 / 122 * 10000) = 1147
  HIGH141 = int(2 * 4 /  68 * 10000) = 1176
```

The pair conflicts in both candidates and neither has a printed hard-register
preference.  The `greg` allocation order and dispositions therefore expose the
priority result directly:

```text
indexed source: ... 125 81 88 159 87 144
                81 in 22; 144 in 23

live only:      ... 126 125 141 81 88 156 87
                141 in 22; 81 in 23
```

Earlier, higher-priority conflicting values already occupy s0 through s5.
`find_reg` scans usable hard registers in increasing order in this CDK build,
which has no `reg_alloc_order` symbol.  The first of this conflicting pair gets
s6 and the second gets s7.  The register swap is thus fully explained without
a compiler-version difference, hidden preference, or constraint.

## Why removing the setup changes the HIGH

In `indexed_copy_source.c`, the nominally dead source cursor setup creates a
complete symbolic address before the loop:

```text
139 = HIGH(D_800E3E48)
133 = LO_SUM(139, D_800E3E48)
176 = 133 + 0xA64                 [indexed copy source base]
144 = 139                         [moved HIGH]
inside loop: a1 = LO_SUM(144, D_800E3E48)
```

CSE has made the early full address useful to the real indexed copy, even
though the source-level `src_cursor` itself has no useful read.  Pseudo 144
only defines the saved HIGH and feeds the lookup address.  Its post-local-allocation
statistics are three weighted references over 70 instructions.

In `indexed_copy_live_only.c`, that early full-address chain is absent.  Loop
motion creates one invariant HIGH/LO_SUM pair for the indexed copy, and the
same HIGH also supplies the lookup address:

```text
141 = HIGH(D_800E3E48)
140 = LO_SUM(141, D_800E3E48)     [indexed copy source base]
inside loop: a1 = LO_SUM(141, D_800E3E48)
```

Pseudo 141 consequently has a definition and two useful consumers.  The
`lreg` dump reports four weighted references over 68 instructions.  The input
pseudo loses only one instruction of live length, so its priority rises from
1138 to 1147; the HIGH rises from 428 to 1176 because four references change
`floor_log2(refs)` from one to two.

Both candidates use the same CDK binary.  Its unstripped `allocno_compare` at
`0x0815d991` directly calls `floor_log2_wide`, multiplies by the reference
count, divides by live length, multiplies by the constant and allocno size,
converts to integer, and sorts the higher result first.  This agrees with
retained `toolchain/gcc-src/2.7.2/global.c:583-608`.  The dump lines are the
same `reg_n_refs` and `reg_live_length` values printed by retained
`flow.c:2884-2890`, and the observed order independently checks the arithmetic.

## Grounded source test and bounded negative

The smallest genuine relationship suggested by this diagnosis was to express
the existing two input-state reads at offsets `0xD4` and `0xD0` as an indexed
member of the input snapshot record inside the third loop, rather than as a
separate mutable cursor initialized with `state + 4` and decremented by four.
`indexed_input_refs.c` tested the equivalent of:

```c
lookup_ptr = input_state_record->lookup_words[slot_index];
```

where `lookup_words[0]` is at `0xD0`.  This is an existing data relationship:
the current two iterations read `state + 0xD4` and then `state + 0xD0`.  It is
not an added use or lifetime constraint.

The positive prediction was that retaining input 81 as the loop's indexed base
would move it from seven to eight weighted references.  The `floor_log2` term
would then rise from two to three and put its approximate priority near 1983 at
the observed 121-instruction live length, safely above HIGH 141's 1176.

The result is a clean negative for that mechanism.  CDK strength-reduces the
typed index to the same `state + 4` derived cursor.  `lreg` still reports input
81 at seven references over 121 instructions, priority 1157, while HIGH 141
remains four references over 68 instructions, priority 1176.  `greg` keeps
HIGH 141 before input 81 and assigns them s6/s7 respectively.  The full result
improves from distance 35 to 30 because the third-loop schedule matches retail
more closely, but the allocator relationship is unchanged.

This exhausts the smallest source-level test supported by the existing dumps.
Another attempt to raise input priority needs new evidence about the source
record or another real input use.  Retaining the stale cursor setup, adding a
dead reference, or constraining a hard register would reproduce an allocation
side effect without reconstructing source semantics.

# Round 47 direct helper-table transfer audit

## Bounded result

No exact transfer was found in the three frozen one-change controls or the two
requested direct-argument follow-ups.  All three current sources independently
reconfirm their recorded exact endpoints.  Each retail body and lineage
fingerprint was read before its candidate was created, and no compiler or
spelling sweep was run.

- `candidate_818A4A64.c` keeps the ordinary `call_data` lifetime, replaces the

- `candidate_818A4948.c` makes the identical transfer from a pinned
  `0x80020000 + 0x5238` construction to `D_80025238`, preserving the ordinary

None is a landing candidate.  Because no candidate was exact, no old/new
recipe cross-check was triggered.  Production sources, callers, recipes,

## Direct-argument follow-up

`candidate_818A4A64_direct_arg.c` removes the `call_data` local and puts
`D_800DEAE0` at the actual helper call.  At recorded `2.8.1-G0` it produces
56/55 words, one substitution, four indels, and distance 5.
`candidate_818A4948_direct_arg.c` puts `D_80025238` directly at its helper call
while retaining `init_data` only for its later registration use; it likewise
produces 59/58 words and distance 5.

The follow-up confirms only half of the prediction.  Moving the symbolic
expression to its actual use moves its materialization after the null branch,
but 2.8.1 leaves a `nop` in the branch delay slot and emits
`lui a1; addiu a1,a1` at generated words 17--18.  Retail fills the branch delay
slot with `lui a1` at word 12 and completes the address at word 15.  The late
materialization also leaves the generated function one word longer.  The
ordinary-local form is closer at distance 3 because it exposes the address
earlier, but it stages the page in `v1`; the direct-argument form exposes it too
late to fill the branch slot.  Neither ordinary source lifetime reproduces the
retail split point, so no helper-prototype rewrite or strict verifier was run.

## Finite inventory

`inventory.json` records all 96 nonrecursive `src/dungeon/*.c` files under
4 MiB that contain both the allocator `func_8003FC64` and render helper
`func_8003DB94`, excluding the fifteen `func_8132*.c`/`func_8133*.c` rows
audited in Round 46.  Thirty-eight have at least one pin and four have a
`NON_MATCHING` conditional.

The exact transfer signature reduced this set to three rows before compiling:
two port arms assign the true static table to the same local that the scored
arm constructs through a pinned page literal, and one row declares a static
table whose address exactly equals its pinned literal arithmetic.  Other
pinned cohort members pass dynamic resources, indexed animation entries, or
already-direct table expressions to the helper; their pins belong to unrelated
position, variant, loop, or callback lifetimes.

## Causal residue

The two `818A` siblings fail in the same three-word address region.
`candidate_818A4A64_regions.txt` shows the ordinary static-symbol assignment
produces `lui v1,0x800e; addiu a1,v1,-0x1520` before the allocation-null branch.
Retail instead puts `lui a1,0x800e` in that branch's delay slot and emits

decomposition for the `0x8002/0x5238` address.  Thus the port-arm source value
is correct, but ordinary 2.8.1 symbol lowering does not reproduce retail's
same-register, mid-branch address lifetime.  This is the next usable
relationship; further table-name spelling changes are not predicted to help.

`8092192C` also has the correct static address value, but removing its pinned
page local changes eleven register assignments in addition to adding one word.
Its address lifetime overlaps the three coordinate copies and offset updates,

The row metadata for both `818A` functions has no `true_name` or proven runtime

The recovered helper definition is `void func_8003DB94(Dst *, Elem *, short)`.

(SHA-256 `2b0dad13de01a1509341f72edf66944bfd30df76190901b9d2d31f276f6f2919`)
and `positive_return_strict.json` (SHA-256

and `e8b3bd1749fa656a4c1e3d78eba90120b163ee861b904413a2a76eac7f954b7b`
respectively.  Relocations were not masked.

## Retail control flow

The complete 58- and 55-word maps in
`work/native_lane/r47_direct_table/retail_818A4948.dis` and
`retail_818A4A64.dis` were read for this review.  In each body, the allocator

machine contract is a nullable allocated-object return.  The positive-form C
is also the source shape that reproduces retail's branch polarity and split
static-address materialization.  The earlier `if (object == NULL)` ordinary C
control had the right value semantics but missed by distance 5 because it
inverted that control-flow shape.

The old sources represented the local jumps as calls to absolute externs marked
`__attribute__((noreturn))`.  That spelling made a relink at any base
non-discriminating and made the native-port failure path falsely fatal.  The
new source returns null directly.  The final-hash `port_review.json` records
that both files compile for the port and have no portability-lint findings.
The generic
arm-identity lander is expected to refuse because the repair intentionally
removes a semantically wrong conditional arm; this is a whole-C semantic
review, not an arm-collapse claim.

## Independent load-region identity

The proposed image relation is:

```
file 0x18C0800 -> VRAM 0x80020000
delta          =      0x7E75F800
```

Three independent observations agree with that relation.

First, it turns both constructor callbacks into exact registered row starts,
and the registered extents form a contiguous chain:

| file row | mapped start | mapped end | role |
|---:|---:|---:|---|
| `0x18C4828` | `0x80024028` | `0x800240C4` | preceding row |
| `0x18C48C4` | `0x800240C4` | `0x80024148` | callback stored by the `4948` constructor |
| `0x18C4948` | `0x80024148` | `0x80024230` | first constructor |
| `0x18C4A30` | `0x80024230` | `0x80024264` | callback stored by the `4A64` constructor |
| `0x18C4A64` | `0x80024264` | `0x80024340` | second constructor |

The recovered `func_818A48C4` body accepts three callback-style arguments.
The `func_818A4A30` machine body reads `a0`, uses `a2` as the target passed to
`func_800478B8`, and ignores the middle word.  Its current `long long` source
spelling is therefore ABI-shaped reconstruction debt; it does not contradict
the ordinary three-word callback role established by the constructor store.

Second, the retail table at file `0x18C4800`, which maps to runtime
`0x80024000`, contains a zero word plus runtime entries `0x800247D4`,
`0x8002488C`, `0x800248D4`, `0x80024DF0`, `0x80024F30`, `0x80024FB0`,
`0x80024FD8`, `0x800250E0`, and `0x80025118`.  Subtracting the same delta maps
all nine entries back into the same file image at `0x18C4FD4` through
`0x18C5918`.  This header/table evidence is independent of interpreting either
constructor's local jump.

Third, two later rows in the same file neighborhood already have byte-exact
true-base promotions under this delta: `0x18C4CA0 -> 0x800244A0` and
`0x18C4ED0 -> 0x800246D0`.  Their promoted candidate hashes are
`f256b619b17274975fa72cdfe5d1dd82f495d11ae1dd6949c58b529422330638`
and `40c98eae76e92b6ecef5af6ccb5083900704f9d5bf67237ccda4f8e994a92ed4`.

The older `dungeon_deep_18c4.overlay.yaml` gate maps a broad synthetic window
and records no row `true_name`; its synthetic `818A` namespace is not identity
evidence.  The two constructor rowbase records were previously only `solved`
because their original pseudo-call sources could not discriminate bases.  The
ordinary local-return candidates supply the missing discriminating recompiles.

## Callee contracts

The final declarations were checked against the recovered resident definitions:

- `src/slus/w_8003FC64.c` defines `void *func_8003FC64(s32 flags)`.  It returns
  an initialized node or null, including explicit null paths for allocation
  policy and exhaustion.  The constructors' positive branch and null return
  preserve that contract.
- `src/slus/code.c` defines
  `void func_8003DB94(struct Dst *, struct Elem *, short)`.  The candidates use
  a `void` return and `s16` third parameter, and pass constant zero.
- `src/slus/w_8004491C.c` defines
  `s32 func_8004491C(RegistrationNode *, s32 registration_id)`.  The candidates
  use `extern s32 func_8004491C(void *, s32)` and explicitly convert the
  address `D_80045340` to the target's 32-bit registration ID.  Its result is
  intentionally ignored.  This replaces the initially exact but incompatible
  `void (void *, void *)` declaration without changing bytes.

The candidates store the two verified same-image callback entry addresses and
the same table/registration addresses as retail.  They add no volatile object,
fake use, inline assembly, register binding, literal-address arithmetic, or
other allocation constraint.

## Caller scope and address collisions

A bounded decode of the mapped local image, file `0x18C4800..0x18C6000`
(runtime `0x80024000..0x80025800`), found one direct call to the first
constructor: `jal 0x80024148` at runtime `0x80024DE0`.  It supplies `a0=s2` and
`a1=s6`, then stores returned `v0` at `0x1C(s2)`, consistent with the
two-argument, pointer-return constructor.  The containing bytes after
`0x800247D4` have no registered source row, so this audit does not invent a
higher-level caller identity or parameter names for them.

The same bounded decode found no direct `j`/`jal` or literal pointer word for
`0x80024264`, and no literal pointer word for `0x80024148`.  That excludes a
plain local function table reference in the inspected image, but it does not
prove absence of dynamically constructed or out-of-image indirect callers.

Bare addresses cannot be treated as family-wide identities: other independently
loaded dungeon regions also contain a `func_80024264`, and the family noreturn
list contains that bare spelling for a different region.  These constructors
must be interpreted with their file row and rowbase region.  No noreturn fact
from another load region applies here.

# Round 47 `818A4A64` null-branch delay diagnosis

## Result

One dump-enabled build of `candidate_818A4A64_direct_arg.c` at the recorded
stock `2.8.1-G0` recipe explains why its table `HIGH` cannot fill the
allocation-null branch delay slot.  This is a property of the current
candidate's synthetic control flow and pins; it is not evidence that retail
used an unusual delay-slot rule.

At `sched2` and `dbr`, the taken thread has this exact order:

| RTL insn | hard register/result | source operation |
| --- | --- | --- |
| 33 | `v0 = 0x80020000` | callback-address page literal |
| 35 | `v0 = asm_operands/v(v0)` | retained `ASM_KEEP(match_v0)` |
| 40 | `v0 += 0x4230` | callback-address low part |
| 60 | `a1 = HIGH(D_800DEAE0)` | helper-table page |
| 65 | `a1 = LO_SUM(a1,D_800DEAE0)` | helper-table low part |

The compiler first rejects insn 33 as a delay-slot candidate.  The opposite
fallthrough block is reported live with `v0` and `sp`, while insn 33 sets
`v0`; this is consistent with the candidate's file-scope
`register u32 match_v0 ASM_REG("$2")` model.  `fill_slots_from_thread`
computes the opposite thread's live resources and cannot move an instruction
that sets one of them.  Separately, the synthetic `noreturn` declaration
causes the fallthrough call to end in a barrier.  `rare_destination` therefore
ranks that path rare, and `fill_eager_delay_slots` tries the taken thread
first.

The exact rejection predicate is not printed in the stock `dbr` dump, so the
mapping above is a static inference from the dumped live set and the retained
2.8.1 source.  It is not a runtime trace of the reorg resource bitset.  The
next fact is unconditional: insn 35 prevents the search from ever reaching
the table `HIGH`.  GCC 2.8.1 `stop_search_p` returns true for any instruction
whose pattern satisfies `asm_noperands(pattern) >= 0`; insn 35 is explicitly
an `asm_operands/v`.  If reorg owns the target thread it may scan past the
rejected insn 33, but it stops at insn 35.  If it does not own the thread, the
first rejection stops the scan earlier.  Neither path reaches insn 60.

The table `HIGH` itself is valid in a branch delay slot.  It is the `high`
pattern, with type `move` and length 1.  The MIPS branch-delay predicate
accepts instructions with `dslot=no` and `length=1`.  Its destination `a1`
does not conflict with the dumped fallthrough live set.  The failure is
therefore scan reachability caused by the earlier pinned callback chain, not
machine eligibility of `HIGH(D_800DEAE0)`.

The final assembly reflects this exactly: the conditional branch has no
compiler-filled delay instruction, while the null-path call uses `move v0,0`
as its own call delay.  At `$L2`, GCC emits the callback literal, the empty
`#APP/#NO_APP` keep, its low add, and only then `lui a1` / `addiu a1,a1` for
the helper table.  Reorg pass 1 reports one of six delay-bearing instructions
with zero delays filled; this conditional is the remaining unsequenced jump
in the final `dbr` RTL.

## Retail qualification and next source relationship

Retail puts the helper-table `lui a1,0x800e` in the allocation branch delay
slot and completes its low part after the branch.  The dump establishes that
the current direct-at-call form cannot reproduce that split while the pinned
callback address chain remains ahead of it.

New region-base arithmetic also makes the candidate's control-flow identity
suspect.  For this 55-word body, the decoded `0x80024320` target is consistent
with a local epilogue after applying the overlay's likely runtime base, rather
than a fatal external callee.  The analogous `818A4948` target has the same
property.  Until the row's true link base is verified, the candidate's
`extern void func_80024320(void) __attribute__((noreturn))`, global `v0`
register variable, and callback keep are reconstruction assumptions rather
than semantic facts.

Accordingly, the useful next relationship is coupled reconstruction of the
null return path and both real static addresses.  If the target is the local
epilogue, ordinary `return NULL` control flow may remove the artificial
global-`v0` liveness and callback keep that currently block the delay search.
This report does not establish that deleting `ASM_KEEP` alone is safe or
sufficient, and no new C form was compiled here.

## Reproduction and provenance

The single diagnostic compile was:

```sh
cd <repo>/work/native_lane/r47_null_delay/raw
<repo>/toolchain/compilers/gcc-2.8.1/gcc \
  -B<repo>/toolchain/compilers/gcc-2.8.1/ \
  -S -O2 -G0 -I<repo>/include -w -da \
  <repo>/work/native_lane/r47_direct_table/candidate_818A4A64_direct_arg.c \
  -o direct_arg.s
```

- Candidate source SHA-256:
  `45f1b59313611669aed23681053fa28bd240952da04353afe52b99a65bf0da33`.
- GCC 2.8.1 `cc1` SHA-256:
  `1a48ec5ac87a146a074a9d66d7a67734a4d1ad56553d02d91e8b71c7fecc2d52`.
- `rtl`, `sched`, `sched2`, and `dbr` SHA-256 respectively:
  `93c8f20e7f3cfaf051a62e4314138525d4af42482f6fafdb14d1cbb0296d717c`,
  `6af34f8daab4375c7b754c4296fa0d840f3a6d67aee041fe58f7226aa50c11cb`,
  `54c6659c3adb2a17a0c9bbcdf41973f29aacb895d1c79c24f1f65606640d68f8`,
  and `7eb23f654c94d78e1cadc6ae5ffc34923dfff9a54b6d2275fc3aecc71baab197`.
- Generated assembly SHA-256:
  `d4730bdaf15e69d866dc8318405fbaf7df72a87a59f920c5c22dae4cc51abb03`.

The unstripped compiler binary contains `stop_search_p` at `0x0818b1ed` and
calls `asm_noperands` at `0x081a2c67`; the call result is tested before the
routine returns the stop decision.  This matches
`toolchain/gcc-src/2.8.1/reorg.c`.  The delay eligibility comes from
`toolchain/gcc-src/2.8.1/config/mips/mips.md`'s `define_delay` and `high`
patterns.  Production sources, recipes, exports, and gates were untouched.

#!/usr/bin/env python3
"""Read-only inventory of fake external noreturn calls that jump inside their own row."""

from __future__ import annotations

import collections
import hashlib
import json
import re
import struct
import subprocess
import sys
from pathlib import Path


ROOT = Path(__file__).resolve().parents[3]
sys.path.insert(0, str(ROOT / "tools"))
sys.path.insert(0, str(ROOT / "tools/gate"))

from common import clean_path, rows  # noqa: E402
from pin_census import CMT_RE, arm_labels, sites_of  # noqa: E402
from pin_sites import fn_bounds  # noqa: E402
from rowbase_identity import region_for  # noqa: E402


RETAIL = ROOT / "build_ovl/work/s3_splat/extract/DUNGEON_DUNGEON.BIN"
ROWBASE = ROOT / "config/overlays/dungeon.rowbase.jsonl"
OUT = Path(__file__).with_name("inventory.json")
KNOWN_CONTROLS = {"dungeon/func_818A4948", "dungeon/func_818A4A64"}
CONTROL_FACTS = {
    "dungeon/func_818A4948": {"old_target": "func_80024210", "pins_removed": 6, "exact_words": 58},
    "dungeon/func_818A4A64": {"old_target": "func_80024320", "pins_removed": 4, "exact_words": 55},
}

NORETURN_DECL_RE = re.compile(
    r"(?m)^[ \t]*(?P<prefix>(?:extern\s+)?[^;{}\n]*?)\b"
    r"(?P<name>func_([0-9A-Fa-f]{8}))\s*\([^;{}]*\)\s*"
    r"__attribute__\s*\(\(\s*noreturn\s*\)\)\s*;"
)
ALIAS_RE = re.compile(
    r"(?m)^[ \t]*#[ \t]*define[ \t]+(func_[0-9A-Fa-f]{8})[ \t]+"
    r"(func_[0-9A-Fa-f]{8})[ \t]*$"
)
CALL_RE = re.compile(r"\b(func_[0-9A-Fa-f]{8})\s*\(")
FUNC_DEF_RE = re.compile(r"\b([A-Za-z_]\w*)\s*\([^;{}]*\)\s*\{")
STRING_RE = re.compile(r'"(?:\\.|[^"\\])*"|\'(?:\\.|[^\'\\])*\'')


def sha256(data: bytes) -> str:
    return hashlib.sha256(data).hexdigest()


def scored_arm_text(text: str) -> str:
    """Keep the normal scored build and blank port/dead arms without moving offsets."""
    labels = arm_labels(text)
    out = []
    for i, line in enumerate(text.splitlines(True)):
        label = labels[i] if i < len(labels) else "both"
        out.append(line if label not in ("port", "dead") else re.sub(r"[^\n]", " ", line))
    return "".join(out)


def mask_preprocessor(text: str) -> str:
    """Blank directives and continued macro bodies before brace/function parsing."""
    out = []
    continuation = False
    for line in text.splitlines(True):
        directive = continuation or line.lstrip().startswith("#")
        continuation = directive and line.rstrip("\n").rstrip().endswith("\\")
        out.append(re.sub(r"[^\n]", " ", line) if directive else line)
    return "".join(out)


def aliases_of(text: str) -> dict[str, str]:
    return {m.group(1): m.group(2) for m in ALIAS_RE.finditer(text)}


def resolve_alias(name: str, aliases: dict[str, str]) -> str:
    seen = set()
    while name in aliases and name not in seen:
        seen.add(name)
        name = aliases[name]
    return name


def function_bodies(text: str) -> list[tuple[str, int, int]]:
    """Return top-level function bodies as (name, body_start, body_end)."""
    masked = CMT_RE.sub(lambda m: " " * (m.end() - m.start()), text)
    masked = STRING_RE.sub(lambda m: " " * (m.end() - m.start()), masked)
    masked = mask_preprocessor(masked)
    depth = 0
    depths = []
    for char in masked:
        depths.append(depth)
        if char == "{":
            depth += 1
        elif char == "}":
            depth -= 1
    out = []
    for match in FUNC_DEF_RE.finditer(masked):
        brace = masked.find("{", match.start(), match.end())
        if brace < 0 or depths[brace] != 0 or match.group(1) in {"if", "for", "while", "switch"}:
            continue
        bounds = fn_bounds(masked, brace)
        if bounds:
            out.append((match.group(1), bounds[0] + 1, bounds[1]))
    return out


def j_target(word: int, pc: int) -> tuple[str | None, int | None]:
    opcode = word >> 26
    if opcode not in (2, 3):
        return None, None
    target = ((pc + 4) & 0xF0000000) | ((word & 0x03FFFFFF) << 2)
    return ("j" if opcode == 2 else "jal"), target


def epilogue_facts(words: list[int], target_word: int) -> dict:
    jr_word = next((i for i in range(target_word, len(words)) if words[i] == 0x03E00008), None)
    if jr_word is None:
        return {"next_jr_ra_offset": None, "next_jr_distance_words": None,
                "lw_ra_before_next_jr": False, "sp_restore_before_or_in_jr_delay": False}
    through_delay = words[target_word:min(len(words), jr_word + 2)]
    restores_ra = any((w >> 26) == 35 and ((w >> 21) & 31) == 29 and ((w >> 16) & 31) == 31
                      for w in through_delay)
    restores_sp = any((w >> 26) == 9 and ((w >> 21) & 31) == 29 and ((w >> 16) & 31) == 29
                      and 0 < (w & 0xFFFF) < 0x8000 for w in through_delay)
    return {"next_jr_ra_offset": f"0x{jr_word * 4:X}",
            "next_jr_distance_words": jr_word - target_word,
            "lw_ra_before_next_jr": restores_ra,
            "sp_restore_before_or_in_jr_delay": restores_sp}


def candidate_paths() -> set[Path]:
    """Let rg perform the only directory-wide source scan, with the required byte cap."""
    pattern = r"func_[0-9A-Fa-f]{8}[^;\n]*__attribute__\s*\(\(\s*noreturn\s*\)\)"
    proc = subprocess.run(
        ["rg", "--max-filesize", "4M", "-l", pattern, "src/dungeon/"],
        cwd=ROOT, text=True, capture_output=True, check=True,
    )
    return {(ROOT / line).resolve() for line in proc.stdout.splitlines() if line}


def main() -> None:
    retail = RETAIL.read_bytes()
    paths = candidate_paths()
    all_rows = list(rows())
    entries = []
    rejected = collections.Counter()

    for row in all_rows:
        if row["container"] != "dungeon" or not row["exists"]:
            continue
        path = clean_path(row)
        if path.resolve() not in paths:
            continue
        source_bytes = path.read_bytes()
        source = source_bytes.decode(errors="replace")
        pins = sites_of(source)
        if not pins:
            rejected["pin-free"] += 1
            continue
        region = region_for("dungeon", row["foff"], proven_only=False, root=ROOT)
        if region is None or region.get("base_confidence") not in {"solved", "proven"}:
            rejected["no-solved-rowbase"] += 1
            continue

        scored = scored_arm_text(source)
        aliases = aliases_of(scored)
        declarations: dict[str, dict] = {}
